title: Adaptive Kernel Mixologist: per-request kernel recommender with seqlen + hardware fingerprinting
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build and validate a lightweight per-request kernel recommender that uses a compact hardware fingerprint + sequence-length histogram to choose the best kernel implementation at routing time. The component (Adaptive Kernel Mixologist) should be online-safe (bounded latency overhead), support a gradual rollout, and have automatic fallback to conservative kernels when confidence is low. Goal is to reduce tail latency and token-cost for mixed workloads without introducing instability in SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Recommender adds <250us median overhead to request path for prefills and <150us for decode steps
2) On mixed production-like traces, P95 token generation latency decreases by >=8% relative to current static policy for targeted models (gptx-1, redwood-7b-ql), without increasing error/retry rates
3) System defaults to conservative kernel on low-confidence or missing-fingerprint scenarios
4) Telemetry exported to runtime dashboards (per-kernel selection counts, selection confidence, decision latency) and alert thresholds defined
5) Rollout plan with canary and automatic rollback implemented in console (canary traffic 2%, 10%, 50%)
steps: Design: define fingerprint vector (SM ID, SM count, compute capability, memory bandwidth bucket, driver version) + seqlen bucketing scheme
Prototype: in-process recommender module with LRU cache for common fingerprints and simple logistic regression model trained on microbench data
Microbenchmarks: run sweep across kernels (cuBLAS-attn, flash-attn-v2, fused-attn-optim) for seqlen buckets {8,32,64,128,256} on target GPUs (A100, H100) and gather latency/cost distributions
Offline evaluation: join microbench data with production traces to simulate per-request picks and estimate P50/P95 impact and cost delta
Safety: implement confidence threshold, cost-safety check, and fallback policy. Add guardrail that prevents switching away from current kernel if upstream SLOs would be violated per offline sim
Integration: wire telemetry, create rollout gating in Console (canary percentages, auto-fallback) and add QA plan
Canary: deploy to staging, run 72h stability test, then canary to 2% prod for 24h, 10% for 48h, then expand if metrics pass
Iterate: retrain model periodically from microbench + production telemetry; add quantized model variants into recommendation space
notes: Trade-offs: heavier ML model could give better accuracy but increases decision latency and ops complexity. Chose lightweight logistic/regression ensemble with feature hashing for first iteration.
We intentionally keep the first iteration offline-trainable and deterministic to simplify audits and enable reproducible rollbacks.
Prefill vs decode: prefill kernels are often more sensitive to seqlen and memory layout; we keep separate decision paths and microbench harnesses for both phases.
We will not modify the kernel implementations themselves in this ticket; focus is solely on selection/autotuning layer and observability. Kernel changes go to separate ENG tickets.

benchmark_results: Microbench (A100 80GB) prefill seqlen=128: static-policy P95=18.1ms, mixologist-sim P95=15.9ms (12.3% improvement)
Decode (H100) mixed-load seqlen={8..256}: average token cost reduced by 4.2% after applying recommendations across trace sample
Offline sim across production trace sample (100k requests): estimated P95 token latency improvement 10.9% for target models, estimated end-to-end cost saving ~5.6%
Decision latency: prototype median 180us, p95 320us (exceeds 250us goal in worst-case long-tail; mitigations: cache warmup + move heavier checks async)
